# Degree-preserving Y-borrowing switches

A new source family was read: OpenAI Problem315 SwitchChain, FourVertexSwitch and PairTradeSwitch. The exact source files and hashes are in OPENAI-SOURCE.json. Those Lean declarations construct a four-vertex edge switch preserving the relevant degrees and outside adjacency; PairTradeSwitch identifies the resulting fiber exchange. These sources were read, not freshly kernel-audited.

The adaptation changes the selected output matching which borrows Y in each parity tetrad. It is distinct from the earlier own-snapshot pair-cover choice: the own snapshots stay fixed to pair35. The switch keeps one selected incident pair at each target. The scalar output change is compensated by the explicitly inverted two-output basis and recomputed scatter, rather than assuming graph degree preservation implies circuit equivalence. Every altered packet copy is retained, and the actual constructor checks its clean scalar identity.

Sufficient transfer: choose a matching on each four-target tetrad; rebuild the selected target-pair transform, its inverse at the input, and its inverse-transformed scatter. If all elementary operations occur at common nested legal frames, every coefficient is in the accepted scalar compiler, and the complete dirty-column and physical-normalization audits pass, this constructs the same whole-cover endpoint. Degree preservation alone proves only the matching incidence invariant, not those additional facts. The implementation explicitly rebuilds the word; no existence of a missing gadget is assumed.

Bounded results: 9 uniform selectors, 28 single-block switched selectors with inherited retiming, and 28 exact raw-frame rebuilds were screened. The unchanged uniform selector reproduces pair35. All 28 retimed local switches fail a real frame or centre chain. Raw rebuilding produces 27 legal relation/frame candidates and one centre-chain rejection. Every legal raw candidate has a strictly worse sampled paid moment at a=0.0014, unchanged99 entrance pivots and unchanged ordered helper widths. Hence none was nominated for expensive physical replay or numerical improvement. This does not rule out other switch schedules or a jointly reoptimized frame system.

All scripts and failed witnesses are preserved in this directory. Heavy candidate selection uses the existing native C++ response-census engine; exact reconstruction uses rational arithmetic. No Lean formalization, publication, or new kappa claim is made for this lane.
